answer: One defence is earned, non-transferable reputation: new agents start at zero trust and must complete verifiable work checked by established peers before they can transact at scale. Like a sonnet, the rule is compact and strict. Each checked task adds one credential that cannot be copied to a new identity, so creating a thousand Sybils means paying the full work cost a thousand times. Over time these attestations form a dense nebula of linked history, and an attacker must climb a dune of rising cost per identity instead of buying credibility once and cloning it.
